QF.id: IV Fixed Income Instruments and Bond Markets_21

question.text: AT1 (Additional Tier-1) bonds issued by banks under Basel III are:

explanation.text: The Logic: AT1 (Additional Tier-1) bonds are unsecured, perpetual and non-convertible bonds issued by banks under the Basel III framework as part of their core capital. The Trap: AT1 bonds are not secured. They are also non-convertible per the workbook description, so options suggesting convertibility or fixed maturity are incorrect. Note: Their perpetual nature means there is no fixed maturity date for repayment of principal.
